medical_device_problem_code: Failure to Sense; Incorrect, Inadequate or Imprecise Result or Readings; Low Readings; Missing Test Results
brand_name: Libre 3+ Sensor and Libre Android App
event_text: During a visit to my diabetes education appointment (b)(6)2026, the nurse asked to see my current glucose reading on my Libre app from my Libre3+ sensor. The app reported a reading of 62 mg/dl and showed a trend of going lower. This was on my left arm. She tested me with a brand new finger stick device True Metrix blood glucose meter after calibrating it. It showed my glucose to be 87 mg/dl which is a difference of 25 mg/dl. She inquired if I was feeling low and if I could tell when I was low on glucose. I told her that I could tell when I was low and that I was feeling fine. As a precaution she had me drink some orange juice and eat a protein bar. I told her of the Phase 1 urgent recall of Abbott Libre app and Libre3+ sensors, which she had not heard of. I had previously reported an issue with a sensor that never started properly, that showed low results immediately and that Abbott told me to leave on overnight to allow it to finish "safety checks" resulting in no data next day and when removed had caused a large hematoma under the skin (3/8" high and same diameter as the sensor ). That hematoma took 10 days to resolve itself. The sensor caused issues as I was eating to bring my glucose up when in reality when I checked with my GT333 Rightest meter fingerstick i was then at 192 mg/dl a difference of 137 mg/dl a highly dangerous difference. I reported the first sensor to my endocrinologist (b)(6) MD who said he had not received any word from Abbott regarding the devices or app. The FDA event details shows the covered sensors only to be in kit exp dates of (b)(6)2025, (b)(6)2026. All of the sensors in the event details show a " manufacturing issue that may cause carbon build up in the sensor resulting in low glucose results". Both of my sensors are from (b)(6)2027 exp lots indicating there is an ongoing issue with the Abbott manufactured devices. Lastly I alternate left and right arm for the placement of sensors to allow recovery time from the sensor spike. I replaced the sensor on(b)(6) with a new sensor. Following my usual alternate placement I used the right arm. I placed the sensor about 1/2 inch closer to the elbow to try to avoid where the hematoma had been. After a few minutes I noticed blood dripping from my arm from the sensor. I managed to stop the flow of blood quickly and wrapped the area with a bandage. The sensor finished its 60 minute warmup and I tested readings against finger sticks which were within +/- 10 mg/dl. ANNEX A: 2460, 1535, 3267, 1559. ANNEX E:1888, 1884, 1905. ANNEX F: 4642. ANNEX G: 510, 4718. This report captures sensor # 1. Reference Reports MW6002508, MW6002509.

health_effect_clinical_code: No Clinical Signs, Symptoms or Conditions
event_text: Abbott Diabetes Care received a MedWatch Report that reported the following information pertaining to an Abbott Diabetes Care (ADC) device: The customer reported that the sensor was placed on the left upper arm 10 days prior. During the night, the device began displaying low glucose readings, despite the customer not lying on the sensor. A confirmatory fingerstick measurement showed a value of 300 mg/dL, while the device indicated hypoglycemia. Upon waking, the application reported a glucose level of 45 mg/dL, but a fingerstick measurement was 340 mg/dL. While on the phone with customer support, the sensor failed with five days remaining, and a message stated that the sensor had failed and a new sensor needed to be inserted. The report noted a significant failure rate, with product details indicating that between 5 and 7 days before the intended 15-day wear period, inaccurate readings or errors often occur, and sensors often fail during this timeframe. The customer reported receiving false low readings as low as 44 mg/dL, while fingerstick results indicated glucose levels of 340 mg/dL. No patient consequences were reported. ADC Customer Service attempted to contact the reporter/customer/HCP 3 (three) times to gain additional details regarding this event; however, all follow-up attempts were unsuccessful. Based on the information provided, there was no report of serious injury associated with this event.
manufacturer_narrative: This issue does not meet reportability criteria; however, it is being reported to the FDA as the complaint was received via User Report.\\An investigation is pending at this time. A follow up will be submitted once all investigation activities are completed or additional information is obtained. \\All pertinent information available to Abbott Diabetes Care has been submitted.
